message:
Now I understand the vulnerability. Let me analyze the UAF:

In `pdf_cache_object`, when `x->type == 'o'` (object in object stream), the code does:
```c
pdf_xref_entry *orig_x = x;
orig_x->type = 'O'; /* Mark this node so we know we're recursing. */
fz_try(ctx)
    x = pdf_load_obj_stm(ctx, doc, x->ofs, &doc->lexbuf.base, num);
fz_always(ctx)
    orig_x->type = 'o'; /* Not recursing any more. */
fz_catch(ctx)
    fz_rethrow(ctx);
```

The issue is that `pdf_load_obj_stm` calls `pdf_load_object` which calls `pdf_cache_object` recursively. During this recursion, the xref table may be reallocated (e.g., via `pdf_get_xref_entry_no_null` which can grow the xref array). This means `orig_x` (which points into the xref table) becomes a dangling pointer. Then `orig_x->type = 'o'` in the `fz_always` block writes to freed memory.

Also, after `pdf_load_obj_stm` returns, the code checks `if (!x->obj)` where `x` is the return value from `pdf_load_obj_stm`. But `x` could also be stale if the xref was reallocated.

Let me look at how the xref table can be reallocated during `pdf_load_obj_stm`. Let me check `pdf_get_xref_entry_no_null` and `pdf_xref_len`.

<｜｜DSML｜｜=execute_bash>
<｜｜DSML｜｜>command</｜｜DSML｜｜>grep -n "pdf_get_xref_entry_no_null\|pdf_xref_len\|pdf_get_xref_entry" /workspace/_work/src/source/pdf/pdf-xref.c | head -30</｜｜DSML｜｜>
</｜｜DSML｜｜>
